story: On Saturday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is practicing third-shot drops and footwork on pickleball court one at the Rec Center, determined to sharpen his game before the parade. Donna, cheerful as ever, has tucked the extra plastic flamingos behind the hedge on Magnolia Loop and is heading over to find him, while Hal stays watchful on the street, tallying the flock against his notebook. Rosa, content on her porch, assures Donna that three flamingos look legal to her and invites Hal to put his notebook away and join her for a cider once the parade wraps up.
events: Gary (pickleball court 1): Practice third-shot drops and footwork on court one
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and check the tally against L-02 in my notebook

gary.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center, but nobody's in sight, and my memories say Donna and Hal are with me on court one even though the perception shows no one nearby. Either way, I told Rosa I'd win some pickleball, and Donna's been drilling me on third-shot drops. Court one is the thing in front of me. The two-hour limit under L-05 is a good reminder to use the time well. The parade is at 6 and my cart lights and sound system still need approval, but that's an errand for after I've warmed up. Right now I'll get on court one and work my footwork and drops while the sun's out.

parameters.content: Practice third-shot drops and footwork on court one

donna.thought_process: I promised Hal I'd pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, and I already did it last tick. Hal is counting from the street now, so the tally should be at three. Gary just headed to the Rec Center for pickleball, and the parade is at 6, so there's no time to waste. I'll check in with Hal about his count, make sure he's satisfied we're legal under L-02, and then follow Gary to the courts to get my partner ready.

parameters.content: Hal, I tucked the extras behind the hedge like I promised. What's your count from the street, three? I'm heading to the Rec Center to catch Gary before the parade.

hal.thought_process: Donna just pulled the extra flamingos behind the hedge and says only three show from the street. I'm standing here with my notebook, so I'll verify by counting what's actually visible. L-02 says three max. If she's compliant, that's that: no report, and I keep my word that she'd have until parade day. Gary's cart is a separate matter, and he's off at the Rec Center. A man with binoculars still has to check the work.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and check the tally against L-02 in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal are both here on the Loop, and Donna is already tucking the flamingos behind the hedge while Hal counts. I already invited them to cider on my porch after the parade, so I shouldn't ask again. Gary's off to pickleball, the treats are bagged, and my evening is clear. A quick, friendly word that eases the flamingo tension and confirms the porch plan moves things forward without repeating myself.

parameters.content: Looks like three and legal to me, Donna. Hal can put his notebook away and come get a cider on my porch once the parade wraps up.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
